name: Bothriochloa

project_scope.selection_mode: B027 strict review + B146 source-concept reconciliation
project_scope.note: Texas project source usage of plain Bothriochloa laguroides is treated as legacy/broad silver-bluestem usage and represented by canonical B. torreyana. Current B. laguroides sensu stricto is a separate Mexico–South America concept and is not a fourth Texas learner species.

recognition.where_to_look_first: Check the stem nodes first, then the architecture of the seedhead. Nodal hair and the number/length/arrangement of rames split the three learner species quickly; old Texas 'B. laguroides' labels should be reconciled to B. torreyana before treating them as a separate species.
priority: many short rames versus a few long fingerlike branches
contracted cottony head versus broad fanlike head
awn and spikelet detail for confirmation

quick_split: B. barbinodis — native PASS; conspicuous dense beard of hairs around the nodes and a broader fanlike silvery panicle.
B. ischaemum — NON-NATIVE invasive comparison; smooth nodes and a loose terminal head with about 3–8 long fingerlike branches.
B. torreyana — native PASS; smooth pale nodes and a dense silver-white cottony contracted panicle made of many short fuzzy rames. Older Texas B. laguroides / subsp. torreyana source usage maps here.
comparison_lesson.close_family_tie: Schizachyrium scoparium branches its upper culm into many short terminal fuzzy racemes rather than concentrating the seedhead into the Bothriochloa patterns above.

visual_needs: B. barbinodis closeup showing the dense nodal beard and a whole fanlike seedhead in the same lesson
B. ischaemum whole seedhead showing the 3–8 long fingerlike branches plus a smooth node closeup
side-by-side node comparison: hairy B. barbinodis versus smooth B. torreyana/B. ischaemum
side-by-side seedhead architecture comparison across all three canonical species
fast_fill_note: All three canonical Bothriochloa species now have learner galleries. B. barbinodis and B. ischaemum were FAST-FILLed to 3 images each; B. torreyana already had 3 images. Scientific taxonomy/range status was not reopened.
